headline: The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,818.93 on Tuesday even with the US 10 year Treasury yield at 5.27 percent, close to a 24 year high, and Brent holding above 100 dollars, and that combination now runs into the RBI rate decision and the September FOMC minutes later today.

summary.us: The S&P 500 rose 0.58 percent to a record 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.45 percent to 27,599.89 as the 10 year Treasury yield eased to 5.27 percent from last week's 24 year high above 5.34 percent and oil slipped back below 100 dollars on the US benchmark. Alphabet's 20 year, 4.3 billion dollar nuclear supply agreement with Constellation Energy for 890 MW of new capacity drove power and uranium names, lifting Cameco 6.35 percent, while Cisco gained 4.54 percent and Broadcom 3.67 percent on AI infrastructure orders.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed 0.98 percent higher at 22,776.10 and Bank Nifty rose 0.76 percent to 55,128.40 on Tuesday, with 32 of 50 Nifty constituents higher as easing crude lifted Reliance Industries 2.66 percent after Jefferies raised its model weight on better refining margins. Trent jumped 12.64 percent on a 23 percent rise in second quarter standalone revenue, foreign investors sold a net 2,961 crore rupees in the cash market against domestic buying of 5,089 crore, and the rupee held at 96.36 to the dollar before the RBI decision at 10:00 am IST today.
summary.global: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 1.1 percent higher at 70,683.98 on Tuesday, back above 70,000 for the first time since early July, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng added about 1 percent to 24,280.56 while mainland China stayed shut for Golden Week. The FTSE 100 rose 0.42 percent to 10,541.70 and the DAX 0.77 percent to 25,449.19, the dollar index slipped 0.19 percent to 101.98, and Brent held near 100.70 dollars as JPMorgan put Gulf crude exports at 17.5 million barrels a day, about 98 percent of pre conflict levels, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
